title: Intelligent Systems
description: Foundations of intelligent systems: agents, search, knowledge representation, expert systems, fuzzy logic and nature-inspired techniques.

topics.title: Introduction to Intelligent Systems and Agents
topics.summary: Intelligent systems are approached as thinking or acting humanly or rationally, with the Turing test as the classic benchmark. An agent perceives its environment through sensors and acts through actuators; a rational agent maximises its performance measure.
subtopics: Approaches to AI: thinking/acting humanly, thinking/acting rationally
The Turing test and Turing's prediction
Schools of thought: human performance, mechanisms, evolution, swarm intelligence
Applications of AI in everyday life and industry
Agent model: environment, sensors, actuators, performance measure
Properties of environments; rational and learning agents

topics.title: Problem Solving and Search
topics.summary: Many problems can be framed as search: an initial state, a goal state, a state space, a successor function and a path cost. Breadth-first search finds the shortest path at a memory cost, while depth-first search may be faster but gives no such guarantee.
subtopics: Components of a search problem: initial state, goal state, state space, successor function, path cost
Uninformed versus informed search
Breadth-first search: completeness, optimality, O(b^d)
Depth-first search and comparison with BFS
Heuristics and the warehouse robot case study

topics.title: Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
topics.summary: Knowledge representation structures information so machines can reason with it, through logic, rules, semantic networks and ontologies. It covers the five types of knowledge and the AI knowledge cycle from perception to execution.
subtopics: What knowledge representation is and what must be represented
Types of knowledge: declarative, structural, procedural, meta, heuristic
Propositional logic and truth tables
First-order logic: predicates and quantifiers
Rule-based reasoning: forward and backward chaining
Semantic networks and ontologies

topics.title: Expert Systems
topics.summary: An expert system emulates a human expert using a knowledge base, an inference engine, an explanation facility and a knowledge-acquisition module. Forward and backward chaining drive its reasoning, and MYCIN is the classic case study.
subtopics: What an expert system is
Architecture: knowledge base, inference engine, user interface, explanation facility, knowledge acquisition
Inference engine operation: forward and backward chaining
MYCIN case study
Expert systems versus human experts; criteria for using them
Case-based reasoning

topics.title: Fuzzy Logic Systems
topics.summary: Fuzzy logic lets truth take any value between 0 and 1, so systems can reason with vague terms such as hot or near. A fuzzy system fuzzifies inputs, applies IF-THEN rules (Mamdani inference) and defuzzifies the result with the centroid method.
subtopics: Classical versus fuzzy logic
Fuzzy system architecture: fuzzification, rule base, inference, defuzzification
Membership functions
Mamdani inference with min/max and centroid defuzzification
Case studies: washing machine, office AC, vehicle speed

topics.title: Neural Networks, Genetic Algorithms and Other AI Technologies
topics.summary: Nature-inspired methods include neural networks, genetic algorithms (selection, crossover, mutation), ant colony optimisation and artificial immune systems. Intelligent agents, natural language processing and hybrid systems complete the toolkit.
subtopics: Artificial neural networks
Genetic algorithms: selection, crossover, mutation
Biologically inspired methods: evolutionary computing and swarm intelligence
Intelligent agents and their types
Natural language processing: uses, advantages and disadvantages
Integrating AI technologies into decision support
